sections.body: Some of the earliest cities grew up beside big rivers, because rivers gave water and fertile soil for farming.
Mesopotamia (Tigris and Euphrates, modern Iraq) gave us one of the first writing systems, cuneiform, around 5,000 years ago.
Ancient Egypt (Nile) built pyramids. The Indus Valley civilisation (modern Pakistan and India) had planned cities with drains. Ancient China grew by the Yellow River.
Later civilisations included Ancient Greece, Rome and the Maya in Central America, who built cities and made calendars.

quiz.q: Why did many early civilisations grow near rivers?
options: Rivers gave water and fertile soil for farming
hints: Even today, farms are often in flat river valleys. Why?
quiz.explain: Rivers provided water and rich soil for growing food.

quiz.q: Which civilisation is famous for planned cities with drains?
hints: The lesson mentions drains and planned cities.
It's in modern Pakistan and India.
Ancient Egypt is known for pyramids. Which one is known for drains?
quiz.explain: The Indus Valley civilisation had well-planned cities with drains.

options: One of the first writing systems
hints: It comes from Mesopotamia, about 5,000 years ago.
People used it to record things, like messages and lists.
Example: pyramids are famous buildings from ancient Egypt, beside the Nile.
quiz.explain: Cuneiform, from Mesopotamia, was one of the first writing systems. It began around 5,000 years ago.
